meaning: Cables are bunched when two or more are grouped together in the same containment or are otherwise so close that the specified separation between them is not maintained.
studyNote: Grouping changes the thermal conditions around the cables, so bunched cables may need to be considered differently when establishing current-carrying capacity.

meaning: A busbar trunking system is an enclosed, modular conductor system using solid busbars separated by insulation, with purpose-made sections such as tap-off, feeder, flexible or expansion units.
studyNote: It is a complete distribution system rather than simply exposed busbars, allowing power to be distributed and tapped off along an engineered assembly.

meaning: A cable channel is a cable enclosure, above or below ground, sized so people cannot enter it but cables or conduits remain accessible along their length during and after installation.
studyNote: Its defining feature is continuous cable access without the channel being a space for people to pass through.
distinction: It differs from a cable tunnel, which is large enough for persons to pass through; the supplied study set does not include a separate cable-tunnel entry.

meaning: A cable cleat is a mechanical support component fitted at intervals to hold a cable or conduit securely in position.
studyNote: Its role is mechanical retention, helping the installed wiring system stay where it is intended rather than providing electrical protection by itself.

meaning: A cable coupler is a detachable connection between two flexible cables, made up of a plug and a connector.
studyNote: It lets flexible cables be connected and disconnected deliberately without treating the joint as permanent fixed wiring.
distinction: The connector is the female-contact part; the plug is the mating pin part.

meaning: Cable ducting is a metal or insulating enclosure installed first so that cables can later be drawn through it; the definition specifically distinguishes it from conduit and cable trunking.
studyNote: It provides cable protection and containment while allowing cables to be installed after the ducting is in place.

meaning: A cable ladder is an open support system with transverse rungs fixed to longitudinal side members.
studyNote: It supports cables mechanically while remaining largely open, which distinguishes it from tray or enclosed containment.

meaning: Cable tray is a cable support with a continuous base and raised edges but no cover; the base may be solid or perforated.
studyNote: It supports and routes cables while leaving them accessible rather than fully enclosing them.
distinction: Cable tray has a continuous base; cable ladder uses spaced transverse supports.

meaning: Cable trunking is normally a closed, rectangular enclosure with a removable or hinged side, used to protect cables and sometimes to accommodate other electrical equipment.
studyNote: It combines routing, mechanical protection and accessible containment in a form that can be opened along its length.
distinction: Unlike conduit, cables can be laid into trunking when its cover or side is removed rather than only being drawn through the end.

meaning: Conduit is a closed part of a wiring system through which cables can be drawn in or replaced from the ends; cables are not inserted laterally along its length.
studyNote: It provides a defined route and mechanical containment for conductors or cables.
distinction: This is why conduit is different from removable-cover trunking, which permits lateral access.

meaning: A connector is the female-contact part of a cable coupler or appliance coupler, fitted to the flexible cable end away from the supply.
studyNote: It mates with the plug while keeping the supply-side and load-side parts of the detachable connection distinct.

meaning: Current-carrying capacity is the greatest current a conductor can carry continuously under the stated installation conditions without its steady-state temperature exceeding the permitted value.
studyNote: It is not one fixed number for a cable in every situation: installation method and surrounding conditions are part of the specified conditions in the definition.
distinction: Do not confuse current-carrying capacity (often written Iz) with design current Ib or the rated current of a protective device.

meaning: A flexible cable is designed, by its construction and materials, to withstand flexing while it is in service.
studyNote: Flexibility is an intended service characteristic, not simply the fact that a cable can physically be bent during installation.

meaning: A line conductor is the energy-carrying conductor of an a.c. system other than the neutral, protective conductor or PEN conductor; the term also covers the equivalent conductor in a d.c. system where applicable.
studyNote: In a single-phase circuit it is commonly the conductor informally called 'live' or historically 'phase', but 'line conductor' is the precise term used in the current guide.
distinction: A neutral can be a live part even though it is not a line conductor. A protective conductor is not intended to carry load current in normal operation.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide explicitly says it uses 'line conductor' instead of 'phase conductor' and 'live part' when referring to a conductor intended to be energized in normal use.

meaning: A live part is a conductor or conductive part intended to be energized in normal use. The historical definition includes the neutral conductor but, by convention, excludes a PEN conductor.
studyNote: The term is wider than 'line conductor': it describes parts intended to be energized, which is important when considering protection against contact.
distinction: A neutral conductor is a live part by this definition even though it is not a line conductor.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide uses 'live part' for a conductor or conductive part intended to be energized in normal use, including a neutral conductor.

meaning: A neutral conductor is connected to the neutral point of the system and contributes to the transmission of electrical energy; the historical definition also covers stated d.c. equivalents.
studyNote: It is a current-carrying circuit conductor in normal service and is distinct from a protective conductor.
distinction: Neutral and protective functions are separate unless the system deliberately uses a PEN conductor.

meaning: A PEN conductor deliberately combines the neutral and protective-conductor functions in one conductor.
studyNote: Because it performs both a normal current-carrying function and a protective function, it must not be treated as an ordinary neutral or an ordinary separate PE conductor.

meaning: A protective conductor (PE) is the broad safety-conductor category used to connect exposed-conductive-parts, extraneous-conductive-parts, the main earthing terminal, earth electrodes or the earthed point of the source as required by the protective measure.
studyNote: CPCs, earthing conductors and protective bonding conductors are different protective-conductor roles within this broader safety network.
distinction: A CPC is not a synonym for every protective conductor: it specifically connects exposed-conductive-parts of equipment to the main earthing terminal.

currentGuide.note: Figure 4.1 of the 2026 On-Site Guide shows the different protective-conductor roles—CPC, main protective bonding, earthing and supplementary bonding—around the main earthing terminal.

meaning: A ring final circuit is a final circuit arranged as a closed ring and connected to one supply point.
studyNote: The line, neutral and protective conductors return to the origin, giving two paths around the ring to points on the circuit.
distinction: A ring final circuit is not the same as a radial final circuit; a spur is a branch from a ring or radial circuit.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide treats ring final circuits as one of the standard final-circuit arrangements and gives associated protective-device, cable-size and maximum-length conditions.

meaning: A spur is a branch taken from a ring final circuit or a radial final circuit.
studyNote: It is a branch connection off the main circuit arrangement rather than a separate definition for a complete final circuit.
distinction: Do not use 'spur' as a synonym for an FCU: an FCU can be used on a spur, but the terms describe different things.
